mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the given quadrilaterals is FALSE?

options.A: A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides.
options.B: In a square, all sides are equal and all angles are right angles.
options.C: A rhombus must have all angles equal.
options.D: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all angles right angles.

mcqs.answer: A rhombus must have all angles equal.
mcqs.explanation: Option C is false because a rhombus is defined only by having all four sides equal; its angles need not be equal. A square is a special rhombus where all angles are right, but a general rhombus can have oblique angles. Options A, B and D correctly describe the respective quadrilaterals.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the hierarchical relationship among squares, rectangles, rhombi and parallelograms?

options.A: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.
options.B: Every rectangle is a rhombus, but not every rhombus is a rectangle.
options.C: Every rhombus is a square, but not every square is a rhombus.
options.D: Every parallelogram is a trapezium, but not every trapezium is a parallelogram.

mcqs.answer: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.
mcqs.explanation: Option A is correct: a square satisfies all properties of a rectangle (opposite sides equal and all right angles) but a rectangle need not have all sides equal. Options B and C reverse the actual inclusions, and while option D is true under the inclusive definition of trapezium, it does not address the specific hierarchy asked, making A the best answer.

mcqs.question: Which of the following definitions accurately defines a quadrilateral?

options.A: A polygon with four sides and four vertices.
options.B: A polygon with four equal sides but not necessarily four vertices.
options.C: A shape with three sides and three angles.
options.D: A three‑dimensional solid with four faces.

mcqs.answer: A polygon with four sides and four vertices.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly states that a quadrilateral is a two‑dimensional polygon having exactly four straight sides and four corner points (vertices). Options B, C, and D describe incorrect or unrelated figures: a polygon must have as many vertices as sides, three sides describe a triangle, and a solid with four faces is a tetrahedron, not a quadrilateral.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify sides, vertices and angles of quadrilaterals
mcqs.question: For any quadrilateral ABCD, which statement is always true?

options.A: The sum of its interior angles is 360°.
options.B: It must have at least one right angle.

mcqs.answer: The sum of its interior angles is 360°.
mcqs.explanation: In Euclidean geometry the interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°, regardless of side lengths or angle measures. Options B and C are not universally true (a quadrilateral can have no right angles and unequal sides), and option D is false because a quadrilateral has four vertices.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral is characterized by opposite sides being equal and parallel while adjacent sides are not necessarily equal?
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and parallel; the adjacent sides can differ in length. A square also meets this condition but additionally requires all sides equal, making it a more specific case. A rhombus has all sides equal, and a trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel and exactly two right angles?
mcqs.explanation: A right trapezium (right‑angled trapezoid) possesses one pair of parallel sides (the bases) and two adjacent right angles at one base. Squares and rectangles have four right angles, while a rhombus may have no right angles unless it is a square.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: Which shape is a parallelogram and a rhombus but not a rectangle?
mcqs.explanation: A rhombus has all sides equal and opposite sides parallel, satisfying the definition of a parallelogram. However, its angles are not required to be right angles, so it is not necessarily a rectangle. A square meets both rhombus and rectangle criteria, while a rectangle lacks equal sides, and a trapezium lacks two pairs of parallel sides.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal and one interior angle of 90°. Which specific quadrilateral must it be?
mcqs.explanation: If all sides are equal (property of a rhombus) and one angle is a right angle, then all angles become right angles, satisfying the definition of a square. A rectangle has opposite sides equal, not necessarily all four; a rhombus need not have right angles; a parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel but may have oblique angles.
